title: Cross-module version orchestration plan and health probes for Terraform VPC stack
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Produce a cross-module orchestration plan and an explicit version matrix that maps Terraform module versions, provider versions, and minimum cloud API surface (eg. AWS provider -> required AWS API versions/features). Deliverables: 1) a machine-readable compatibility matrix (CSV/JSON) that CI can consume, 2) CI gating jobs to detect unsupported pin combinations, 3) a canary selection heuristic and automated health probes for preflight/post-upgrade validation, and 4) an operator-facing runbook that details safe pin rotation, drift detection, and rollback criteria. Motivation: We have recurring incidents during private VPC upgrades when module/provider pins drift across services (routing, LB, IAM, VPC endpoints). This ticket centralizes orchestration so upgrades are predictable and automatable for Dedicated and Private customers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Compatibility matrix exists in repo (infra/compat/matrix-2026-03.json) and is generated from authoritative sources for modules/providers.
2) CI job 'tf-compat-check' fails if a PR introduces a pin combination not listed in the matrix.
3) Canary selection policy implemented: selects 2 non-production VPCs per region with low traffic and a reconciliation window.
4) Health probes (smoke plan/apply + service-level smoke tests) run automatically during canary and report to Console.
5) Runbook and rollback steps are drafted, reviewed by SRE and Security, and published to Confluence.
6) No customer-facing outage observed in staged upgrades across 3 canaries during test cycle.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Inventory - gather current pins from terraform state across all private VPC stacks.
Phase 1: Matrix generation - create initial mapping of module versions to supported provider versions and minimal cloud APIs. Commit to infra/compat.
Phase 2: CI integration - add tf-compat-check to PR pipeline and protect main branch.
Phase 3: Canary automation - spin canary VPCs, run smoke apply, then apply real upgrades with health probes.
Phase 4: Gradual roll - use rolling strategy by region and account tiers, with automated pause on health regression.
Phase 5: Postmortem/metrics - measure drift, failed plan percentages, and MTTR to inform next iteration.
testing_steps:
- Create a synthetic canary VPC with test workloads that exercise LB, autoscaling, IAM, and endpoints.
- Run terraform plan/apply against canary with new pins. Verify full apply success and that service-level smoke tests pass.
- Introduce a known incompatible pin in a feature branch and confirm CI 'tf-compat-check' blocks merge.
- Run chaos variant: simulate a partial failure (eg. LB update fails) and confirm rollback plan triggers and health checks detect failure within 5 minutes.
- Verify metrics and logs flow into Console with a custom 'upgrade-health' dashboard.
rollback_plan:
- If health probes fail during canary, automatically run terraform apply with previous pinned versions using saved state snapshot.
- If rollback apply fails, escalate to on-call SRE and open incident runbook (link in infra_artifacts).
- Pause subsequent canaries and notify product and customer success for impacted customers.
- After rollback, perform root cause analysis; do not advance the global pin rotation until fix is validated.

decision_log: Adopted a centralized JSON matrix stored under infra/compat/ to be the single source of truth.
CI gates will be blocking by default; exceptions can be requested and logged via an ephemeral approval flow.
Canary heuristic: select VPCs with <10% median CPU and <5% outbound traffic relative to peak; prefer test accounts isolated from paid customers.
notes: Trade-offs: A strict pinning policy reduces drift but increases maintenance overhead when providers release breaking changes. We chose an operator-driven rotation cadence (monthly) with emergency windows for security fixes. Future work: automate provider release ingestion and propose safe upgrade bundles based on observed module interop tests.
